title: Audit log ingestion and storage optimization for RBAC v2 / SSO admin events
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem statement: As we roll out RBAC v2 and ramp SSO/SAML admin activity, audit traffic has increased 4x for some customers and the current pipeline is a major cost and query-performance pain point. We need a hardened ingestion pipeline plus a long-term storage/retention plan that satisfies compliance (per-tenant retention policies), keeps query latency predictable for console/admin investigations, and controls storage costs.

Goals: 1) Durable, low-latency ingestion of audit events (admin actions, RBAC changes, SSO/SAML auth events) with per-event integrity and metadata enrichment. 2) An indexing and partitioning strategy that supports fast searches for recent windows (hot) and cost-efficient long-term storage (cold) while meeting retention SLAs. 3) Cost controls: tiered retention, sampling/aggregation for noisy event types, and cross-tenant quota enforcement. 4) Maintainability and operational clarity: ILM, clear runbooks, and diagnostics for dropped/skipped events.

Constraints and non-goals: We must keep the audit stream tamper-evident and KMS-integrated. This ticket does not modify console UX for log search (follow-up). We will avoid re-architecting RBAC v2 event schemas in this ticket; schema changes will be handled in ENG-7471.

Proposed design summary:
- Ingestion: Kafka topic (audit.events) with strict schema (Avro) and Schema Registry. Producers (API servers, auth proxies) write enriched events; a lightweight buffering layer (Vector or Logstash) performs last-mile enrichment (tenant_id, region, request_id) and writes to two sinks in parallel: 1) OpenSearch audit cluster for hot indices; 2) S3 raw-archive (gzip + snappy) for immutable long-term storage. Write-ahead to Kafka ensures durability.
- Indexing/partitioning: Time-based daily indices for hot data with tenant prefix: audit-<tenant>-YYYY.MM.DD. For tenants with <1M events/day we roll to weekly indices to limit index churn. Use tenant-level index templates for mappings: keyword fields for actor/principal, event_type, resource_id; nested-free design to optimize indexing and prevent mapping explosions.
- ILM & retention: ILM policies move indices: hot (0-7d) -> warm (8-90d, slower nodes, reduced replicas) -> cold (90-365d, freeze or searchable snapshots) -> delete or move to S3 after tenant-specific retention. For compliance customers, we create a retention profile that keeps immutable S3 raw-archive for 365+ days and locks it via S3 Object Lock when requested.
- Cost controls: per-tenant ingestion quotas enforced in Kafka via token-bucket throttles at producers; high-volume event types (health-check pings, polling) are sampled at source with deterministic sampling keys for reproducibility. Implement an aggregation pipeline for ultra-high-volume events (rollup counts per minute) that keeps detail only for anomalous spikes.
- Query pattern optimizations: Common admin queries target recent 7-30 days and specific tenant IDs. We create tenant-routing aliases (write alias + read aliases) and warm node caching for console queries. Ad-hoc forensic queries hitting cold data should be redirected to S3 raw-archive rehydration job (as background fetch) with a warning to the user about latency/cost.
- Security & integrity: All events encrypted with customer/KMS where applicable. Sign events with HMAC at producer to detect tampering. RBAC v2 changes and SSO/SAML admin flows have dedicated event types and policy version in the record to simplify audits.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Spike (2w) - verify Kafka throughput and Vector transformations; benchmark OpenSearch cluster sizing for 50k events/sec peak. (Owner: Mateo)
2) Schema + Registry (1w) - finalize Avro schema and add compatibility rules. (Owner: Priya)
3) ILM + Index Templates (1w) - create templates, policies, and test rollover. (Owner: Liam O'Connell)
4) Sampling & Quota enforcement (2w) - implement deterministic sampler in auth proxy and per-tenant quota counters in ingestion layer. (Owner: Sofia Martinez)
5) S3 raw-archive + rehydration tool (2w) - write pipeline to write compact raw blobs and a rehydration job to reconstruct events for ad-hoc queries. (Owner: Mateo)
6) QA & compliance review (2w) - retention profile verification and KMS audit. (Owner: Ava Chen)

Rollout strategy: Canary 5% traffic for internal tenants -> 20% customer preview -> allow per-tenant opt-out/retention overrides. Monitor cost delta and query latency.

Trade-offs considered: 1) Single monolithic index vs tenant-prefixed indices: tenant indices reduce blast radius but increase cluster metadata; we will use tenant prefix only for customers above an events threshold and shared indices with tenant_id field for small tenants. 2) Immediate full indexing vs archival-first (raw to S3 then index on-demand): chosen hybrid because we need recent fast search but cannot index everything long-term.
comments: 2026-02-16 Mateo Rivera: Spike started — validated Kafka 1.8 cluster can sustain 60k eps on benchmark nodes; need to increase partition count for audit.events. Observed high GC on a single ingest node when bulk size > 5k.

2026-02-22 Priya Kapoor: Schema v1 posted to Confluence + Registry link. Marked event 'auth.saml.login' and 'rbac.binding.change' as required fields. See confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Audit+Event+Schema
2026-02-27 Liam O'Connell: Draft ILM policies in GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1247 — requesting review from storage team for warm/cold node sizing.
2026-03-03 Sofia Martinez: Implemented deterministic sampler in auth-proxy. Early tests show 8-12% reduction in load on heavy tenants with very noisy events.
2026-03-07 Ava Chen: Compliance review scheduled — S3 Object Lock flow approved for enterprise retention profiles. Need KMS access audit (ENG-7382) to finish.
2026-03-10 Mateo Rivera: Running canary with internal tenants at 5% — no dropped events. Next: add per-tenant quota alerts and cost dashboard card.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline ingests at target throughput 50k events/sec in benchmark with <1% drop for 10m sustained.
Hot index query latency (99th) for 7-day window < 500ms for typical admin queries.
ILM policies move indices through hot->warm->cold correctly and searchable snapshots restore within SLA.
Per-tenant retention override can be configured and enforced; S3 raw-archive retention obeys Object Lock when enabled.
Cost dashboard card shows per-tenant audit storage and ingestion costs and alerts when budget thresholds exceeded.
Security/compliance sign-off obtained and KMS access audited (ENG-7382).
